# Daily AI Newsletter Digest - Saturday, 7 November 2026

## 🔥 Top Stories
1. **Anthropic accelerates R&D and discloses acquisition of Mithril Medicine for AI-driven drug discovery** — This matters because it showcases Anthropic's expanding efforts in AI research and its potential to disrupt the pharmaceutical industry with AI-driven drug discovery.
2. **Google makes Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available, adding support for 15-second video clips and cutting prices by 30%** — This matters because it expands accessible multimodal video capabilities for developers, making AI-powered video creation more affordable and accessible.
3. **Dropbox agrees to acquire AI infrastructure startup Tigris Data for $350 million** — This matters because it highlights the growing demand for AI infrastructure and Dropbox's strategic move to strengthen its position in supporting large-scale AI systems.
4. **Meta launches live video calls with its Muse AI avatar** — This matters because it introduces a new form of interactive AI experience, combining real-time voice generation with lip-synced avatar rendering, potentially changing how we interact with AI avatars.
5. **Perplexity launches always-on Teammates AI agents** — This matters because it positions Perplexity as a competitor in the enterprise AI agent market, offering persistent AI agents for workplace tasks and potentially transforming how teams work with AI.

## 🤖 AI Models & Research
- Anthropic R&D accelerates, with a focus on AI models like GPT-6 Cyber, indicating a push towards more advanced and secure AI technologies.
- The Beam model from Reflection AI on the Ollama platform will start requiring usage credits or a subscription after November 9, 2026, marking a shift towards monetization of AI model usage.

## 🛠️ Tools & Products
- Ollama offers a significant discount on usage credits with its plans for regular users of the Beam model, providing a cost-effective solution for those who plan to use AI models extensively.
- Inkling 2 Small is mentioned as part of the AI landscape, suggesting ongoing development in compact or specialized AI models.

## 📰 Industry News
- Waymo cuts ties with Uber, and Agility lists on NASDAQ, indicating significant movements in the autonomous vehicle and robotics industries.
- Texas data centers are at risk, which could impact the infrastructure supporting AI and tech operations in the region.
- The acquisition of Tigris Data by Dropbox and Anthropic's acquisition of Mithril Medicine highlight the consolidation and strategic expansion in the AI and tech industry.

## Ollama Newsletter

**Priority: MEDIUM**

### Top Updates
- The free period for Beam, a model from Reflection AI, on the Ollama platform is ending on Sunday, November 9, 2026. After this date, using Beam will require either usage credits or a subscription, with pricing set as follows: $0.125 per 1M tokens for input, $0.015 per 1M tokens for cached input, and $0.40 per 1M tokens for output. This change affects all users who have been utilizing Beam for free since its launch on October 16, 2026, and they will start receiving payment-required errors for their requests unless they add credits to their account.
- Users can add usage credits to their account using a credit card, a process that can be completed in a few minutes. For those planning to use Beam regularly, Ollama offers a significant discount on usage credits with their plans, which can be found on the Ollama pricing page.
- The Beam model page and pricing details are available on the Ollama website, providing users with all the necessary information to plan their usage and manage their costs effectively.

### Notable Links
- Beam: https://ollama.com/library/beam
- Add usage credits: https://ollama.com/dashboard
- Pricing and plans: https://ollama.com/pricing

Waymo, Alphabet’s autonomous-driving company, plans to end its exclusive Uber partnership in Austin and Atlanta in January 2028 and begin offering rides through its own app in those cities. Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana said rider feedback drove the decision: customers wanted a more consistent booking experience, while requests through Uber did not guarantee that a Waymo vehicle would be dispatched. Uber says it may continue hosting Waymo rides as long as both companies agree, so the change ends exclusivity rather than necessarily ending all integration.[1][2][3]

The move reflects Waymo’s shift from using established ride-hailing platforms to owning more of the customer relationship, demand data, and service experience as its robotaxi network scales. Waymo reportedly operates about 4,000 vehicles, provides more than 500,000 weekly trips across 14 cities, and already uses its own app in other markets.[9] Strategically, the decision intensifies competition between Waymo and Uber: Uber can still provide distribution and fleet utilization, but Waymo’s direct channel may strengthen its brand and economics while allowing Uber to work with additional autonomous-vehicle providers. It also highlights a broader AI/ML industry trend in which autonomous-driving companies are moving from technology demonstrations toward large-scale, consumer-facing operations.[2][12]
additionalContext.source: Los Angeles Times, TechCrunch, Bloomberg News, Waymo, and Uber

additionalContext.context:
Uber’s latest AI/ML developments span both internal productivity and autonomous mobility. In November 2026, Uber announced a company-wide rollout of ChatGPT Work through ChatGPT Enterprise, while its engineering organization highlighted AI applications such as real-time traffic forecasting, responsible-AI governance, and using data from billions of trips to train systems for Level 4 autonomy. Uber’s broader ML platform supports core functions including pricing, matching, routing, fraud detection, and customer support, alongside partnerships with autonomous-vehicle companies.[3][4][5][8]

The key industry development is Waymo’s decision to end its exclusive Uber arrangement in Austin and Atlanta in January 2028, earlier than the partnership’s reported May 2028 expiration. Waymo plans to let customers request rides directly through its own app, citing a desire for more consistent access; Uber says Waymo vehicles may continue operating on Uber’s platform if both companies agree. The shift matters because it increases direct competition between the two companies over robotaxi customers and highlights a strategic tension in autonomous mobility: Uber provides marketplace scale and operations, while Waymo increasingly wants direct ownership of the rider relationship and service demand.[9][10][14][15]

Agility Robotics became the first U.S. publicly listed pure-play humanoid-robotics company on November 5, 2026, after completing its business combination with Churchill Capital Corp XI. Its shares trade on Nasdaq under AGLT, with warrants under AGLTW. The transaction raised approximately $465 million in gross capital, including a PIPE led by Foxconn, giving the company funding to scale production, fulfill customer orders, and invest in robotics, physical-AI software, safety systems, and manufacturing infrastructure.[1][8][14] Agility’s core product is Digit, a bipedal humanoid designed for industrial material handling and warehouse tasks. The company says it has more than $300 million in committed multi-year Digit 5 orders, nine customers using its robots, and a commercial pipeline exceeding 30 prospective customers.[3][5][14]

The listing matters because it gives investors public-market exposure to humanoid robotics while offering Agility capital and visibility during a formative stage for physical AI. Recent commercial momentum includes an expanded GXO Logistics deployment at facilities in North Carolina and Tennessee, with additional deployments expected to begin in 2027, plus a planned AGCO agricultural-equipment pilot. Digit 5 is positioned as a cooperatively safe humanoid capable of operating near people without conventional safety cages. The industry impact is significant but unproven: Agility’s public debut may accelerate competition and enterprise adoption, while its valuation, manufacturing scale-up, safety performance, and ability to convert pilots and commitments into profitable deployments remain key execution risks.[3][7][13]

Anthropic is an AI company developing Claude, a family of large language models and agentic systems aimed at coding, knowledge work, scientific research, and other complex tasks. Its latest significance is the apparent acceleration of AI-assisted AI development: an independent assessment by the Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR) group found that Anthropic’s benchmark capabilities improved about 1.9 times faster after October 2025, implying roughly two years of historical progress in the past year. METR cautioned that this measures performance on well-specified tasks, not general intelligence, and that the finding is based partly on confidential company data and interviews.

The development matters because Claude is increasingly being used in the research and engineering pipeline that produces more capable models, potentially creating a feedback loop in which AI speeds experimentation, coding, evaluation, and model optimization. Anthropic’s recent activity includes the introduction of Claude Opus 5.5, expanded scientific and drug-development initiatives, and reports that Claude optimized more than 30 open-source biomolecular models in under four weeks, averaging roughly fourfold speedups. The contrast between rapid technical progress and calls from Anthropic leadership to slow AI’s pace has intensified debate over evaluation, safety, controllability, and whether governance can keep up with capability gains. Sources: METR, Reuters, Associated Press, and Anthropic’s newsroom and research publications.

GPT-6 is OpenAI’s latest model family, introduced in 2026 with general-purpose models such as GPT-6 Sol and Luna, followed by specialized variants including GPT-6.1 and GPT-6 Cyber. The most relevant recent development is GPT-6 Cyber, announced November 5, 2026, which is designed to find, reproduce, and help fix software vulnerabilities while more reliably remaining within authorized testing boundaries. OpenAI reports a 48.5% score on ExploitGym, up from 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, and says the model identified 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities and developed 948 Linux privilege-escalation exploits during research.[1][2]

The model matters because it combines substantially stronger offensive-security capability with safeguards intended to limit misuse. OpenAI classified GPT-6 Cyber as “Critical” under its Preparedness Framework and initially restricted access to approved cybersecurity customers through its API and Codex. This could accelerate vulnerability discovery, patch validation, and defensive research, but it also raises the stakes for access controls, monitoring, and responsible disclosure because the same capabilities could be misused. GPT-6’s broader rollout across ChatGPT and developer products signals increasing competition around specialized, agentic AI systems, particularly in cybersecurity, where capability and operational safety must advance together.[2][3]
additionalContext.source: OpenAI, “GPT‑6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents” (November 5, 2026); SecurityWeek coverage (November 6, 2026)

missingStories.headline: Google makes Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available
missingStories.summary: Google released Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash broadly, adding support for 15-second video clips and cutting prices by 30% compared with Omni 1.1. The update expands accessible multimodal video capabilities for developers.
missingStories.whyItMatters: Practitioners gain a cheaper production option for video understanding and multimodal applications, increasing competitive pressure on other model providers.

missingStories.headline: Dropbox agrees to acquire AI infrastructure startup Tigris Data for $350 million
missingStories.summary: Dropbox announced plans to acquire Tigris Data, which develops distributed storage for AI workloads across multiple clouds. The transaction would be Dropbox’s largest acquisition and targets infrastructure demands created by large-scale AI systems.
missingStories.whyItMatters: The deal highlights storage and data infrastructure as strategic bottlenecks for AI workloads and may affect how practitioners design scalable, multi-cloud training and inference systems.

missingStories.headline: Meta launches live video calls with its Muse AI avatar
missingStories.summary: Meta made live video calls with its Muse AI avatar available to all users in the United States. The experience combines real-time voice generation with a lip-synced avatar-rendering model.
missingStories.whyItMatters: This is a notable consumer deployment of real-time multimodal AI and provides practitioners with a reference point for latency, avatar rendering, and voice-video synchronization requirements.

missingStories.headline: Perplexity launches always-on Teammates AI agents
missingStories.summary: Perplexity introduced Teammates, a product built around persistent AI agents for workplace tasks. The launch positions Perplexity against enterprise agent offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic.
missingStories.whyItMatters: Always-on agents shift AI products from conversational assistance toward continuous task execution, raising practical questions about permissions, monitoring, reliability, and operating costs.

missingStories.headline: Anthropic discloses acquisition of Mithril Medicine for AI-driven drug discovery
missingStories.summary: Anthropic disclosed that it acquired Mithril Medicine, a one-person biotechnology company whose founder used Claude to coordinate a drug-development program across external laboratories. Anthropic also reported early results from several pharmaceutical partners and plans to expand this model.
missingStories.whyItMatters: The move signals a shift from selling general-purpose models to operating domain-specific scientific programs, with implications for AI-enabled research workflows, validation, and biotech partnerships.
